Ablation findings: why the ViT is behind the CNN

results/encoder · 23 Nov 2026 · ViT variants with the MLP predictor and the reference loss, each changing one thing from LeWM's per-frame ViT · 3 seeds × 32,768 steps, float32, batch 128 · held-out metrics on 1,332 windows from the 333 reserved episodes. Controls cnn-mlp-ref, vit-mlp-ref, vit-mlp1-ref and the anchors are reused from results/main.

Snapshot, 10 of 11 variants. vit_p4 (4×4 patches) ran out of GPU memory at its first step on an 8 GB GTX 1080 and has no results. vit_d192 has 2 of 3 seeds; the third is still training. All numbers are the team's local proxies on held-out training-corpus episodes, not the hidden leaderboard evaluation.
In short
  • The gap comes from how the frames enter the encoder. A ViT that sees the 3 frames together reaches 69–73% held-out top-1. LeWM's ViT embeds each frame on its own and reaches 22%.
  • Space-time attention (vitst) closes 92% of the gap, reliably: 69.1% ± 1.3 on all three seeds.
  • Stacking the frames as channels (vitstack) can match the CNN but is unstable: one seed reaches 72.9%, two get stuck at 34%.
  • Nothing else about the per-frame ViT matters. Learning rate, patch size, embedding size and projector normalization all land within 1 point of 22.1%.
  • The CNN is still the best encoder (73.0%, identical across seeds, and the fastest to train).

1. The variants

vit_lnLayerNorm instead of BatchNorm in the projector3 × 65does the BatchNorm projector hurt?

The clip encoders (vitstack, vitst) give one embedding per 3-frame window, as the CNN does, so their MLP predictor is exactly the reference predictor. The per-frame variants give 3 embeddings, and the MLP sees all 3.

2. Seeing the frames together closes the gap

EncoderHow the frames enterTop-1Gap closedMotion R²BlendActions 1st of 8
cnn (target)stacked as channels73.0% ± 0.0100%0.9441.02592.7%
vitstall frames' patches attend jointly69.1% ± 1.392%0.9090.97693.6%
vitstackstacked as channels47.0% ± 22.4
seeds 34% / 73% / 34%		49% (one seed 100%)0.4520.54673.5%
vit (baseline)each frame on its own, 3 embeddings to the MLP22.1% ± 0.20%0.9350.64877.8%
vit + mlp1each frame on its own, newest only to the MLP24.9% ± 0.15%0.8530.61977.0%

Gap closed = (top-1 − 22.1%) / (73.0% − 22.1%). The per-frame ViT cannot be fixed by giving the predictor more frames: the frames have to meet inside the encoder. Both ways of doing that in a ViT work, and joint space-time attention is the reliable one. vitst matches the CNN on use of actions (93.6%) and has a lower prediction error (nMSE 0.051 vs 0.067). It is lower on motion R² (0.909 vs 0.944), which costs it about 0.05 of blend.

3. Stacking works, but two of three seeds get stuck

vitstack's seeds separate between steps 2,000 and 5,000. Seed 1 climbs to 0.94 in-batch top-1 and matches the CNN at every horizon (72.9% held-out). Seeds 0 and 2 settle at 0.50 in-batch top-1, reach 34% held-out (still above the per-frame ViT) and lose most of their motion R² (0.20–0.22). This is the same 0.50 in-batch plateau as the stuck seeds of cnn-ar-ref in main and every seed of ref_nonce in the loss suite. Stacking gives the ViT what it needs, but training it this way is unreliable.

4. Nothing else about the per-frame ViT matters

KnobLowervitHigher
Encoder learning rate (5e-5 / 2e-4 / 1e-3)21.5% ± 0.522.1% ± 0.222.5% ± 0.7
Patch size (4 / 8 / 16)out of memory22.1%22.6% ± 0.3
Embedding size (48 / 96 / 192)21.6% ± 1.022.1%21.5% ± 1.0 (2 seeds)
Projector norm (BatchNorm / LayerNorm)22.1%15.4% ± 11.0
seeds 22.5% / 2.7% / 21.1%

Held-out top-1. Every working variant lands within 1 point of the baseline. A per-frame ViT converges to about 22% whether it trains 4× faster or slower, has 2× more or fewer dimensions, or uses half as many tokens. The limit is the per-frame design, not its settings.

  • Coarser patches are free. 16×16 patches give the same results as 8×8 with 4× fewer tokens, and trained fastest of the ViTs (104 min per seed). Whether finer patches help is still open: vit_p4 needs a GPU with more than 8 GB.
  • LayerNorm in the projector hurts. All three seeds stall at about 0.17 in-batch top-1. Two escape around step 12,000–14,000 and end at the baseline; one never does and ends at 2.7% held-out. Keep BatchNorm.
  • Smaller and slower is also slower to start. vit_d48 and vit_lr5e5 leave the early plateau thousands of steps later than the baseline (one vit_d48 seed at about step 13,000) but reach the same end point.

5. The other metrics

  • Top-1 measures dynamics, not episode recognition: encoder-only retrieval is about 1% for every variant.
  • Embeddings use more directions when the frames meet in the encoder: effective rank ends at about 48 for vitst and for vitstack's good seed, versus about 40 for the per-frame baseline and about 100 for the CNN (of 256 dimensions; the ViTs have 96).
  • Cost. vitst took 200 min per seed on a TITAN RTX, against 83 min for the CNN on an RTX 2080 Ti (only vit_d192, at 357 min, cost more). Its ONNX file is smaller (4.4 vs 5.7 MiB), and every variant passed test_submission.py. GPUs differ between jobs, so treat times as rough.

6. Caveats

  • Only the MLP predictor and the reference loss were tested. The loss suite shows twice the InfoNCE weight gives the CNN about 1 more point; this was not tried with the ViTs.
  • Every variant keeps LeWM's other settings (optimizer, schedule, projector); vitst and vitstack were not tuned.
  • vit_p4 is missing, and vit_d192 has 2 seeds.
  • Three seeds give a spread, not a confidence interval. For vitstack they cannot say how often the good outcome happens.
  • Local proxies only; the hidden evaluation may weigh things differently.

7. What this suggests

  • Keep the CNN encoder. It is still the best, the most stable and the cheapest to train.
  • If a ViT is wanted, make it a clip encoder. vitst is the reliable option (69%). vitstack shows a ViT can match the CNN, if its seed instability is fixed (e.g. warm-up or a lower learning rate early on).
  • Do not tune the per-frame ViT further: five knobs moved it by at most 1 point.
  • Understand the 0.50 in-batch plateau. It appears in vitstack, cnn-ar-ref and ref_nonce, and is the main source of seed failures across the ablations.
  • To finish the suite: rerun vit_p4 on a GPU with more memory (e.g. with --constraint), and regenerate this report once vit_d192's third seed is done.
